description: D14 (knowledge half): close koine's zero written engagement with two prior-art bodies that sit closest to KGP — nanopublications / Trusty URIs and Frictionless / Data Package — and re-found ADR-0006 on the stronger justification the prior-art sweep surfaced. TODAY ADR-0006 justifies keeping the bespoke TSV + content-addressed-claim canonical largely on fit grounds; the decisive argument is structural and external: RDFC-1.0 is defined over RDF 1.1 ONLY, has no defined behaviour for RDF 1.2 triple terms, and revising it is EXPLICITLY out of the RDF/SPARQL Working Group's charter (which runs to 2027) — the W3C canonicalization stack cannot, today or on any published schedule, canonicalize the structure KGP needs. Lead the ADR with that. The nanopublication comparison is the other half and is the sharpest statement of what KGP is: a Trusty URI hashes ALL FOUR graphs (head + assertion + provenance + pubinfo), so two labs asserting the IDENTICAL triple mint DIFFERENT URIs — the identifier fingerprints a publication event. KGP §3 hashes the CLAIM ALONE, with provenance travelling beside the claim as a repeated record and never entering its identity, so independent producers CONVERGE on one claim id (§3.3) and their provenance merges onto it. That inversion is exactly what makes cross-producer merge work and is what a Trusty URI cannot do by construction. Frictionless / Data Package is cited and dismissed: it standardizes file packaging and table schemas, and discharges no clause of KGP §3 (claim identity) or §7 (confidence / license / egress). The prose is already drafted in docs/positioning.md (Prior art considered section) — this tasklist lands the NORMATIVE half in ADR-0006 and specs/grounding-pack.md §3.4. Lifecycle per specs/README.md: KGP is candidate (0.5.0); a §3.4 rationale edit is non-normative-in-effect but still gets a version bump + dated changelog entry, and claim identity (§3, §3.3) MUST be byte-unchanged. Agnostic: bind roles, no product names in normative text. ROADMAP.md Phase F7.

userStories.title: Re-found ADR-0006 on the RDFC-1.0 / RDF 1.2 charter argument
userStories.description: Amend ADR-0006 so its Decision/Rationale LEADS with the structural, externally-verifiable reason KGP cannot delegate canonicalization to the W3C stack, rather than with fit or preference. The existing decision (bespoke TSV + content-addressed claim canonical retained; RDF-star / PROV / JSON-LD are a specified, round-trip-tested projection) does NOT change — only the justification's ordering and strength.
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-0006's rationale leads with: RDFC-1.0 is defined over RDF 1.1 only and has NO defined behaviour for RDF 1.2 triple terms, and revising it is explicitly out of the RDF/SPARQL Working Group charter (which runs to 2027) — so the W3C canonicalization stack cannot canonicalize the structure KGP needs, today or on any published schedule.

The amendment is recorded as an amendment (dated, with a short 'what changed and why' note), not a silent rewrite: the original decision, its date, and its status are preserved and the outcome is explicitly unchanged.

A re-open test is stated: the concrete upstream event (a chartered, published canonicalization defined over RDF 1.2 triple terms) that would reopen the decision — consistent with the re-open test already in specs/grounding-pack.md §3.4.
The ADR names no product as a normative actor and adds no dependency on any private/instance repo (CLAUDE.md rule).

userStories.title: Nanopublications / Trusty URIs — cite the nearest ancestor and state the inversion
userStories.description: Add the nanopublication comparison to both ADR-0006 and specs/grounding-pack.md §3.4. This is the sharpest available statement of what KGP's identity mechanism IS, and koine has zero written engagement with it today.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/grounding-pack.md §3.4 (and ADR-0006's context) states that a Trusty URI hashes all four nanopublication graphs — head, assertion, provenance, pubinfo — so two producers asserting the identical triple mint DIFFERENT identifiers, because the identifier fingerprints a publication event.

The same text states KGP's inversion normatively-consistently: §3 normalization covers the claim's subject / relation / object / world ONLY, provenance travels beside the claim as a repeated record and never enters claim identity, and therefore independent producers CONVERGE on one claim id (§3.3) with provenance merging onto it — the property cross-producer merge requires and a Trusty URI cannot provide by construction.
The text is explicit that nanopublications are the better model where the unit of interest is the publication, and KGP's unit of interest is the claim — a scope difference, not a quality claim.
§3 and §3.3 are byte-unchanged: claim identity does not move. A verification step in the story's notes records the before/after check.
